title: Case, new grad technical program manager, weak answers

questions.text: RouteBuddy shows campus shuttle locations. Students say the shuttle times are wrong. How would you find out why?
Estimate how many students use the shuttle on a weekday at a campus of 15,000 students.
Launch is in two weeks. Engineers say the live map and arrival alerts need three weeks. What do you do?
Who are the users of RouteBuddy and what do they need first?
How would you know the launch worked?
Estimate how many phones open RouteBuddy at 8 a.m.

turns.speaker: interviewer
turns.text: Hi Bao, I'm Carla, a technical program manager. This is a thirty minute case conversation, spoken only.

turns.speaker: candidate
turns.text: Hi Carla, thank you for meeting me.

turns.speaker: interviewer
turns.text: Are you still in school, or have you graduated?

turns.speaker: candidate
turns.text: I graduated in May. I am looking for my first job.

turns.speaker: interviewer
turns.text: Okay. I will ask three cases about a campus shuttle app. Think out loud, and ask me anything you need.

turns.speaker: interviewer
turns.text: RouteBuddy shows campus shuttle locations. Students say the shuttle times are wrong. How would you find out why?

turns.speaker: candidate
turns.text: I would check the app and see if the times are wrong. Maybe the GPS is not good. Then I would tell the engineers to fix it.

turns.speaker: interviewer
turns.text: Where in the system could the wrong time come from?

turns.speaker: candidate
turns.text: The GPS device on the bus could be wrong, or the server, or the app on the phone. I would compare the real bus time to the app time for one route.

turns.speaker: interviewer
turns.text: Estimate how many students use the shuttle on a weekday at a campus of 15,000 students.

turns.speaker: candidate
turns.text: Fifteen thousand students. Maybe half use the shuttle. So about seven thousand students every day.

turns.speaker: interviewer
turns.text: Do half of all students really ride every day? What would change that number?

turns.speaker: candidate
turns.text: Maybe not. Some students live on campus and walk. I would say fewer, maybe a thousand. I am not sure how to check.

turns.speaker: interviewer
turns.text: Launch is in two weeks. Engineers say the live map and arrival alerts need three weeks. What do you do?

turns.speaker: candidate
turns.text: I would tell the engineers to work faster and add more people. Then we can launch both features on time.

turns.speaker: interviewer
turns.text: Suppose you cannot add people. What would you do?

turns.speaker: candidate
turns.text: I would launch the live map first because students need it most, and delay the alerts by a week. Then I would tell the team and the users about the date.

turns.speaker: interviewer
turns.text: Thanks. What questions do you have?

turns.speaker: candidate
turns.text: What does a new program manager do in the first month?

turns.speaker: interviewer
turns.text: They shadow two projects, write one status report a week, and take one small project by week four.

turns.speaker: interviewer
turns.text: That is our time, Bao. The recruiter will follow up within a week.

turns.speaker: candidate
turns.text: Thank you, Carla.

notes: Weak for new grad: short generic answers, no estimate reasoning, but a reasonable scope cut after a probe.
